abstract.text: The host-injection channel for the actor’s team memberships, which are stamped onto
every usage service and Amplitude event so MAU reporting can slice by team without a
later join against billing-service (#3130).

Uses weak linking to XCTest, allowing the framework to work in both test and non-test contexts.

Note: This class conforms to XCTestObservation protocol at runtime but doesn’t declare it
to avoid linking against XCTest.
Lets a downstream integration (WebDriverAgent, the Desktop Mobile Analyzer) declare
which product is driving the current process, so Amplitude can distinguish an
Appium-driven scan (and its major version) from a customer calling the SDK directly.
A set of options for when a rule is run on a view.
A summary of one rule being run on one view.
The accessibility traits on a view.  Similar to UIAccessibilityTraits.
Lives within AxeResult and contains meta data about the scan, device information, the screenshot, and the view hierarchy.

This class contains all the information from one accessibility scan of a screen.  This is a Swift representation of the JSON sent to the axe DevTools Mobile server (if using UI automated tests or manual tests). This can be used to assert number of accessibility failures and passes on one screen.  It also contains the view hierarchy of what was scanned and which rules were run.
Downstream products that can explicitly identify themselves to the framework.
One team membership of the actor driving this process.
